name: Faster AI: GPU Rooflines, Agent Learning & Homa’s Fast Transport Protocol
description:
**Monday, October 19, 2026 · 9:00–10:00 AM PDT · Online**
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
Join us for three perspectives on AI performance: getting more from GPUs, turning agent failures into learning, and exploring faster network transport.
**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: Why Does Serving More Users Change GPU Utilization?**
by Rajat “Raj” Dandekar, Co-founder of Vizuara
In this 5–10 minute technical segment, Raj will use a visual explanation and code to explore how concurrent users change GPU utilization. He’ll connect vLLM measurements on an H100 to the roofline model and briefly introduce Vizuara’s Kernel Engineering workshop.
**Bio:** Rajat Dandekar is a co-founder of Vizuara. He holds a PhD in Mechanical Engineering from Purdue University and BTech and MTech degrees from IIT Madras.
**Talk #2: From Agent Traces to Agent Training: Closing the Continuous Learning Loop**
by Rustem Feyzkhanov, Engineering Manager at Snorkel AI
Production traces show where agents fail, but how do we turn those failures into learning? This talk explores a practical loop from traces to reproducible simulations, verifiable rewards, and model improvement through fine-tuning or reinforcement learning. We’ll also look at when it’s better to change prompts, tools, or the agent harness instead of updating model weights.
**Bio:** Rustem Feyzkhanov is an Engineering Manager at Snorkel AI.
**Talk #3: Homa: A Fast Lane for Small Messages**
by John Ousterhout, Professor Emeritus of Computer Science at Stanford University
John will explain how Homa can dramatically reduce small-message latency and explore its potential relevance to AI workloads. Drawing on his expertise in transport protocols, he’ll discuss what Homa could offer when small-message latency matters. Its importance for AI workloads remains an open, workload-dependent question.
**Bio:** John Ousterhout is a Professor Emeritus of Computer Science at Stanford University, the creator of Tcl, and a systems researcher whose current work focuses on the Homa transport protocol.
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
**Related Links**
Github Repo: [http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/](http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/)

name: Breast Cancer Prevention, Screening & Treatment
description:
Presented by Kaiser Permanente and the Greater Baltimore Committee Baltimore Women and Allies Board (BWAB) 
Building Better Health Together, an engaging monthly virtual series, is designed to inspire healthier lifestyles and empower participants with the knowledge, tools, and resources they need to thrive. While part of this series focuses on topics that uniquely effect women’s health and well-being, it also explores a broad range of health and wellness issues relevant to everyone. We welcome all those who want to learn and advocate for healthier families, workplaces, and communities. Through dynamic discussions with health experts, participants will explore today’s most relevant wellness topics, including preventive care, mental health, stress management, nutrition, healthy aging, work-life balance, and more. This isn’t your typical health webinar. Each session is designed to be informative, interactive, and inspiring, combining expert insights with practical strategies that attendees can apply in their everyday lives. Whether you’re looking to prioritize your own well-being, support the women in your life, or learn how healthier individuals contribute to stronger communities, Building Better Health Together offers a welcoming forum for learning, connection, and growth. 
What to Expect:

Expert-led wellness conversations
Actionable tips and tools for everyday health
Q&A sessions
Resources to support physical, mental, and emotional well-being
A welcoming environment for all participants

Run of Show – 12:00 – 12:45

Welcome and Introductions
Health Chat
Q&A
Wrap up

In this event led by Dr. Amy Gillis, MD, Radiation Oncologist, attendees will learn about breast cancer risk factors, screening recommendations, the benefits of early detection, and treatment options that can lead to better outcomes.

name: April Ryan: "Notes on a Blacklash"
description:
Notes on a Blacklash is veteran White House reporter April Ryan’s gripping, soul-baring look at what happens when the world suddenly turns its full attention on you. This isn’t just the story of one viral moment with President Trump. It’s about the avalanche that follows: the scrutiny, the emotional and physical toll, and the way your identity can become fuel for headlines and hashtags.

 

April pulls back the curtain on what it truly costs to be seen and what it takes to survive it. With vulnerability and power, she recounts the moments that made her go viral, not because she chased attention, but because she showed up authentically. Her presence, her truth, and her refusal to shrink under pressure struck a chord and sparked cultural firestorms.

 

From a high-stakes press room showdown to the history-making decision by Vice President Kamala Harris, from the public disrespect of Stevie Wonder to the slap heard around the world, April explores how race, gender, and power collide in a world addicted to outrage and instant opinions.

 

At its core, this book explores visibility—its price, its power, and the fight to reclaim your story when millions are watching. What does it mean to go viral when your hair is politicized, your voice is policed, and your very existence is treated as a threat? Sometimes, this is what it feels like when the spotlight finds you: uninvited, unrelenting, and impossible to ignore.

 

About the Author: 

April Ryan is a renowned journalist, author, and political analyst. She hosts The Tea with April on Substack and has authored Black Women Will Save the World and Under Fire. Based in the surrounding Baltimore area, Ryan continues to amplify critical conversations on race, gender, and politics.

name: Marcia Chatelain: "How Bright the Path Grows"
description:
There is no shortage of footage immortalizing the men who spoke at the 1963 March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, when 250,000 Americans gathered beneath the Lincoln Memorial to call for an end to segregation. There were reverends and rabbis, activists and Rat-Pack icons—and of course the day’s headliner, whose prophetic dream of a post-Jim Crow world has forever defined the Civil Rights Movement. But there is no “class photo” of the Black women who helped organize the march, performed on its main stage, or were honored during its “Tribute to Negro Women Fighters for Freedom.”

 

In How Bright the Path Grows, Marcia Chatelain weaves a gleaming group portrait of these singular women. Among this cohort were several household names: vaudeville icon Josephine Baker; civil rights activist Rosa Parks, gospel legend Mahalia Jackson, and Daisy Bates, champion of the Little Rock Nine. But many were relative unknowns, including Eva Jessye, the choir director who designed the day’s musical program, and Anna Hedgeman, the coordinator who pushed in the eleventh hour for a tribute to Black women’s work.

 

How Bright the Path Grows is a scintillating group biography, rendering the lives of thirteen Black women visionaries—some famous, others soon to be—in novelistic detail and like never seen before.

 

Marcia Chatelain will be joined in conversation by award-winning journalist and author Elaine Weiss. 

 

About the Author: 

Marcia Chatelain is a Presidential Penn Compact Professor of Africana studies at the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of South Side Girls and Franchise, which won the 2021 Pulitzer Prize in History, the James Beard Foundation Book Award for Writing, the Hagley Prize for Business History, and the Lawrence W. Levine Award from the Organization of American Historians. An active public speaker and educational consultant, Chatelain has received awards and honors from the Ford Foundation, the American Association of University Women, and the German Marshall Fund of the United States.

 

About the Moderator: 

Elaine Weiss is an award-winning journalist, author, and public speaker. She is the author of Fruits of Victory: The Woman’s Land Army of the Great War; The Woman’s Hour: The Great Fight to Win the Vote, and her most recent book, Spell Freedom: The Underground Schools that Built the Civil Rights Movement.  Elaine lives with her husband in Baltimore, Maryland. Find out more at ElaineWeiss.com.

name: Serving Up Wisdom: Witch's Brew: True Tales and Folklore of Witchcraft in Colonial Maryland
description:
Space for this program is limited; registration required. If you are registering a group larger than two individuals, please contact the Programs department at pao@prattlibrary.org or 410-396-5494.

 

This program is recommended for individuals 55+; however, all are welcome. 

 

Join us for Enoch Pratt Free Library’s free luncheon series, which offers patrons an afternoon of engaging conversations, performances, and activities. Pratt is excited to work in partnership with several community organizations to bring in a variety of dynamic presenters and performers, with rich academic and artistic backgrounds to lead these programs.

 

What’s on the menu:

 

We are thrilled to welcome Amanda Hughes, Manager of the Social Sciences and History Department. Just in time for Halloween, we will delve into the eerie depths of Maryland's witchy past! Hear true tales and folklore from across the state and find out what Colonial Maryland was really like for those accused of witchcraft.

 

Can you tell fact from legend?

 

Following the presentation, participants may also choose to take part in other facilitated activities or join our regular book discussion group led by Pratt Librarians from the Fiction Dept.

 

Lunch will be provided.

 

Please contact the Programs department at pao@prattlibrary.org or 410-396-5494, if you have questions about registration or to request accommodations.

name: Meditations for Modern Life:  Wednesday Mornings
description:
These classes include both meditations and teachings based on Buddha’s wisdom that can help us to stay peaceful, even in the most challenging times. Current series topic is posted on our website:
[Wednesday 11am Meditation Class — Kadampa Meditation Center Maryland | Baltimore](https://www.meditationmd.org/wednesdays)

**To Register for In-Person Class:** Please register at the door (please arrive 15 minutes early).
**Cost:** $12/class ($8 students/seniors 62+/unemployed).
Your first class is always free.
You can also [become a member](https://www.meditationmd.org/memberships) starting at $50/month and receive discounts while you help to provide a steady level of support for our activities. These classes are included in your membership!

**With Resident Teacher, Gen Kelsang Chogden**
Gen Chogden is an American Buddhist nun and the Resident Teacher of Kadampa Meditation Center Maryland. Gen Chogden has been practicing Kadampa Buddhism since 1998 under Venerable Geshe Kelsang Gyatso, who gave her the title “Gen” indicating that she is a senior ordained teacher of the Kadampa Tradition.
Gen Chogden is well-loved for her warmth, kindness, and wisdom, which have come from her sincere and heartfelt practice of Kadam Dharma over many years.
Her teachings are always practical and easy to apply to everyday life. Through her gentle and joyful approach and her peaceful example, she has helped many people find true happiness in their hearts.

name: JOIN US FOR THE CRC ROUNDTABLE – Striped Bass and Striper and Rockfish, Oh My!
description:
Striped bass are central to the culture, economy, and ecology of the Chesapeake Bay to the entire Atlantic Coast; their importance is reflected in the sheer number of monikers they have collected, from striper to rockfish. Given their regional significance, understanding their population dynamics and emerging concerns for management are crucial to protecting this iconic species for generations to come.
Join us on Wednesday, October 21st from 12-1pm to learn about striped bass surveys and recreational fishing in the Chesapeake Bay.

name: EPA Tools & Resources Webinar Partnering to Address Lead (Pb)
description: EPA works with the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO) and the Environmental Council of the States (ECOS) under a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on projects to protect public health from environmental threats and hazards and strengthen environmental health systems across the country. EPA and our state partners work collaboratively in tackling priority environmental challenges facing the nation, including lead (Pb). Over the past year, ASTHO and ECOS hosted regional calls with state environmental and health agencies to discuss cross-agency lead coordination. This webinar will provide an overview of what was heard at the listening sessions – including overarching themes, state program highlights, and call outcomes – as well as plans to build upon this work in the coming year.

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
Fall Focus: Starting Strong — School, Service Year & What Comes Next!
Fall is a season of new beginnings! As young people head back to
school, college, training programs, and work — and our newest Maryland Corps / Service Year members begin their year of service —
TouchPoint
threadHOURS
is here to help everyone start strong and stay on track.
Each Wednesday at threadHOURS, young people can get hands-on support navigating the opportunities and challenges that come with a new school or program year. Whether they need help adjusting to a new schedule, staying on top of school or Service Year expectations, connecting to resources, solving a problem before it becomes a barrier, or thinking ahead to their next academic or professional step, threadHOURS is a place to check in, get connected, and keep moving forward.
For our
Maryland Corps / Service Year members
, threadHOURS is also a place to stay connected throughout the year — celebrating wins, troubleshooting challenges at their host sites, accessing additional resources and opportunities, and making sure their year of service is building toward what comes next.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
The beginning of a new school, work, or service year is a great time to reconnect with your young person. Ask what they’re excited about, what feels challenging, and what would help them start the year strong. Come to threadHOURS together to make a plan, tackle a next step, or connect with someone who can help.
You don’t need to have all the answers — showing up, asking questions, and helping your young person navigate the transition is exactly the relational scaffolding they need.

name: Alliah Agostini: "The Ten Tins"
description:
Shiny blue cookie tins promise a delicious bite. But what’s inside this one? A sewing kit? Old photos? Shiny car keys?

 

From Teta to Nai Nai, none of the grown-ups seem to know that tins are for cookies! Will this group of friends ever find their treat?

 

Based on the cultural phenomenon of putting random items in cookie tins, this paper-over-board picture book is a hilarious page turning read aloud, perfect for the holiday season or anytime reading.

 

About the Author: 

Alliah Agostini is the author of many picture books and easy readers for children including Junior Library Guild Selection Big Tune: Rise of the Dancehall Prince , Black KidLit Award-winning The Juneteenth Story: Celebrating the End of Slavery in the United States, Oprah Winfrey: A Little Golden Book Biography, The Juneteenth Cookbook, Great Idea Malia, Blexi, Play!, Scarecited on the First Day of School, No Cat Like Tac, Art's Art, and more.  ​Alliah resides in New Jersey  with her husband and two children. She has an A.B. and an M.B.A. from Harvard.

 

About the Program:

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 3pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Free street parking is available along the side of the building.

name: Meditations for World Peace

**This class includes guided meditations, a teaching, and chanted prayers for world peace.**
We can all do something to contribute to world peace! In this class, we are creating world peace in two main ways. We are making prayers together for world peace, and we are also creating inner peace. Without inner peace, outer peace is impossible. When we create peace within our own mind, it ripples out to create peace in our world.
“If everyone were to practice cherishing others, many of the major problems of the world would be solved in a few years.” -Venerable Geshe Kelsang Gyatso, How to Transform Your Life

name: Chronically ChILL Weekly October Social
description:
About the Event

Living with chronic illness can be isolating — especially when it feels like no one truly understands what you’re going through. That’s why we created Chronically ChILL, a social group for chronically ill people who just want to connect, talk, and be themselves.

Our socials are a relaxed, judgment-free space to simply be human and enjoy the company of others who get it. There’s no agenda, no pressure, and no need to talk about symptoms unless you want to. It’s just about making friends, laughing a little, and finding community.

Come as you are — camera optional, pajama friendly, cozy vibes welcome.

⸻

What to Expect
• Easygoing conversation and good company
• A warm, understanding community
• Zero pressure to perform or overshare
• The chance to actually socialize and make new friends who understand the ups and downs of chronic illness

Whether you join for ten minutes or the full hour, you’re part of the ChILL community.

***In order to join the Zoom call, your zoom username MUST match your Meetup name.***

⸻
☕ What to Bring
• Yourself, exactly as you are
• Snacks or drinks if you'd like
⸻

Who It’s For

Chronically ill, disabled, and neurodivergent individuals looking for friendship, laughter, and connection in a relaxed online environment.

You don’t have to be “doing well” to show up — you just have to show up.

name: Ladew Fall Lectures: Black Flora: Floriculture and the Art of Living (Ladew Topiary Gardens)
description:
Maryland author, Teri Speight will share a deep dive into the book, Black Flora, and what it should mean to the world of Floriculture. Often overlooked or missing out on opportunities to be seen, 25 Black farmers, florists, and creatives heard the call of flowers. As they individually answered the call, each one has gone to bloom in their own way. From expanding their business portfolio to changing their vision, the portraits of these pioneers should show the world they are not a monolith, but a culture proudly coming out of the shadows. Teri will share three special profiles, her experiences, and how she is continuing the conversation about Black Flora. 
Teri is currently a garden writer, podcaster, garden experience curator, visionary, and former estate gardener. Teri is the founder of Cottage in the Court, which offers curated garden experiences for small groups, and one-on-one garden coaching, specializing in earth-friendly practices.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: What Drove Witch Hunts
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“What Drove Witch Hunts,”** on past centuries’ persecution of those accused of sorcery, with Larissa "Kat" Tracy, medievalist and visiting assistant teaching professor of English at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/what-drove-witch-hunts](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/what-drove-witch-hunts) .]

The witch trials of late medieval and early modern Europe and early colonial America have inspired fear and horror for centuries. They left behind questions we still struggle to answer, such as: What sparked belief in witches? What compels societies to seek out and persecute those supposedly in command of darkness?

Hear such questions tackled by Dr. Larissa Tracy, a medieval literary historian who has appeared on several History Channel documentaries on medieval torture and brutality and given several excellent Profs and Pints talks in the past.

Although the witch hunts have been metaphors in the modern era for tyranny and corruption, the real history of witchcraft and the witch hunts lies in the desire for power and control, as well as genuine fear that the Devil walks among us, she’ll explain.

Although we frequently think of the witch hunts as a medieval phenomenon, accusations of witchcraft escalated after the Reformation, during the early modern period. Dr. Tracy will discuss how kings, queens, and witch-finders general all played a role in the torture and execution of innocent women and men. Those targeted included herbal healers, religious heretics, dissidents, social rivals, and marginalized members of society.

Exemplifying the darker aspects of human society, the witch hunts culminated in some of the most tragic events in history. The history of them still holds important lessons for today. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID. Bar doors open at 5 pm. The talk starts at 6:30.)

name: CA Board of Directors Meeting
D.L. Hughley: "Charlie’s Boy"
description:
**THIS PROGRAM IS SOLD OUT** 

 

The long-awaited memoir by the comedy legend and author of multiple New York Times bestsellers, a beautiful and mesmerizing book that reveals as never before his childhood in South Central Los Angeles, his time in the infamous Bloods gang, and how humor became his salvation.

 

I learned a joke could be more than humor. It was body armor. Could be a spell. Could be a sword and a shield, all in one breath.

 

He was always Charlie’s Boy—even before he found his name, his voice, his fame.

 

In this raw, cinematic, and deeply personal memoir, acclaimed comedian and cultural critic D.L. Hughley documents his rise from the streets of South Central Los Angeles to the national spotlight—and the man who quietly stood behind him through it all.

 

While his mother’s wrath shaped his early years with fear and rejection, it was Charlie Hughley—a soft-spoken bag handler at the Los Angeles Airport—who raised D.L. and taught him how to survive through tough love and sacrifice. Though he was not D.L.’s biological father—a fact only revealed when D.L. was ten—Charlie gave his boy the only thing he truly needed: a sense of being seen.

 

It was a time when gangs ruled the streets of South Central, and D.L. rose through the ranks of the Bloods. But when his mother’s car was shot up and dead roses were left on his doorstep—signaling he was marked for death—D.L.’s mother knew that he couldn’t stay in Los Angeles. So, D.L. boarded a bus to Ohio and left behind everything he understood. It was exile. But it proved to be a fresh start.

 

This is not just a coming-of-age story. It’s the story of how one man found his voice by being raised in silence—and how he learned to get on stage and turn pain into punch lines. Through storytelling that’s both unsparing and funny, Charlie’s Boy is a tribute to the man who never asked for one, and a reckoning for the boy who had to wrestle for love, identity, and truth.

D.L. Hugley will be joined in conversation by Karsonya Wise Whitehead, host of Today with Dr. Kaye on WEAA 88.9 FM.

About the Author: 

D.L. Hughley is one of “The Original Kings of Comedy.” He hosts the national radio program The D.L. Hughley Show, which is syndicated in more than sixty markets. His comedy specials have appeared on HBO, Netflix, Comedy Central, and Showtime. His satirical documentary special, DL Hughley: The Endangered List, received the prestigious George Foster Peabody Award. He created and starred in the ABC sitcom The Hughleys. He is the author of the New York Times bestsellers How Not to Get Shot and Black Man, White House. How Not to Get Shot was selected as a finalist for the Goodreads Choice Awards and the Audie Awards. D.L. lives with his family in Los Angeles, California.

 

About the Moderator:
Karsonya Wise Whitehead is the host of Today with Dr. Kaye on WEAA 88.9 FM. She is the founding director of The Karson Institute for Race, Peace & Social Justice, as well as a communication and African and African American Studies professor at Loyola University.

All registered in-person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last.  There will not be a book signing following the program. name: Find a Startup to Help or Join
description:
**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

description:
Learn about water quality testing with the scientists of Blue Water Baltimore! An Outfall Screening Blitz consists of taking teams of volunteers into our local streams to sample water quality. The events take place 48 hours after a major rain event to ensure stormwater is not being sampled. Samples will be collected from streams being monitored where dry weather flow is coming from a stormwater outfall. We will discuss different types of pollution, how it is entering our waterways and steps you can take to help report and prevent pollution from happening.

name: Angela DiTerlizzi: "A Very Scary Book"
description:
From NYT bestsellers Angela and Tony DiTerlizzi comes a humorous, social-emotional story about not judging a book by its cover—even if that cover is super scary!

 

Up in the attic where no one ever goes, there lives a very scary book. He might look scary, but all he wants is a friend. When, one day, he feels brave enough to venture downstairs, he ends up frightening the other books. Will Scary ever be able to find a friend who sees him for who he truly is?

 

Angela and Tony DiTerlizzi, the bestselling husband-and-wife team behind A Very Cranky Book, have crafted a tale that is both a friendship story and social-emotional fable. It’s the perfect reminder that sometimes good friends can come in unexpected packages.

 

About the Author: 

Angela DiTerlizzi is a beloved author of award-winning, charming, and inspiring picture books, including the New York Times and USA Today bestselling The Magical Yet series, Some Bugs, Just Add Glitter, and many others. Her books have been featured in Entertainment Weekly and BuzzFeed, on the Today show, and in Cheerios boxes.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 1pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last.Free street parking and bike parking available.If you need additional accommodations, please let us know at events@prattlibrary.org or 443-768-0762.

description:
Hawk Watch at the Susquehannock Wildlife Conservation Center from 9 am-2 pm.

Co-leaders John Garrison & Elaine Scribner-Wagner (517-622-1211 authorelainescribner@gmail.com)

Join us as we search for migratory south-bound raptors at the hawk watch platform at the Susquehannock Wildlife Conservation Center (1725 Trappe Church Rd, Darlington, MD 21034). We will meet at 9am and walk the trails around the property in search of migrating songbirds as we make our way to our hilltop hawk watch platform. Once we reach the hawk watching platform we will sit or stand and tally migrating raptors as they fly through the Deer Creek Valley. You must join the group for the hike at 9am but you do not have to stay the entire time. Please bring plenty of water, snacks, some comfortable footwear, and outdoor clothing. Target birds for the trip include Broad-winged Hawk, Sharp-Shinned Hawk, and other raptors.

name: Susquehannock Wildlife Society: October Open House
description:
Join us for our Monthly Open House at the Susquehannock Wildlife Conservation Center! This free event is a wonderful opportunity to explore our conservation Center, enjoy the beauty of the Deer Creek Valley, and learn about the wildlife and natural habitats of the Lower Susquehanna Region.

Visitors are welcome to tour our facilities, immersive ecosystem exhibits, visit our scenic wildlife viewing platform, and meet the staff and volunteers behind our wildlife conservation, research, and education programs. Whether you're interested in learning more about local wildlife, attending future programs, becoming a member, or simply spending time in nature, our Open House is the perfect way to get connected.

Stop by, ask questions, and discover how the Susquehannock Wildlife Society is working to conserve wildlife in the Lower Susquehanna region and beyond.

name: NEC Drop-in: Outstanding Opossums
description:
October’s theme, Nocturnal Animals of Cylburn, focuses on animals that become active as the sun goes down. Each Saturday will highlight a different nocturnal animal that calls Cylburn Arboretum home and explore the adaptations that help them thrive at night. While some creatures of the night sometimes get a spooky reputation, we’ll shed some light on these often misunderstood animals and discover there’s much more to admire than fear!

Please note: NO live animals will be present during these programs.

All ages are welcome. No fee or registration required (supplies limited). Drop-in anytime between 11am to 12pm.

October 3: Observant Owls

Whooo’s awake when the sun goes down? Drop by the Nature Education Center to discover the owls that call Cylburn home and uncover the adaptations that make these nighttime hunters so well suited for life after dark. 

October 10: Remarkable Raccoons

There’s a ‘masked’ visitor roaming Cylburn after dark! A raccoon’s distinctive black mask provides camouflage and helps reduce glare. Drop by the Nature Education Center to find out more about the adaptations that help them thrive at night.

October 17: Fantastic Flying squirrels

Something is soaring through the trees but it isn’t a bird or a bat! Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about how these small nocturnal mammals glide through the forest after dark. 

October 24: Outstanding Opossums

What’s lurking around Cylburn after dark? It might be an opossum!  Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about the only marsupials in North America and how they help the environment.

October 31: BOOtiful Bats

This Halloween, discover the bats that fly over Cylburn after sunset. Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn how these nocturnal mammals navigate the darkness and play an important role in our ecosystem.

### 🎥 CSTGIA 2026 – Week 28

From Strategic Cyber Foresight to Adaptive Cyber Enterprises: Building Organizations That Learn Faster Than Threats Evolve

Artificial intelligence is accelerating. Cyber threats are evolving. Critical infrastructure is converging. Traditional planning cycles are no longer sufficient.

In Week 28 of the Cyber Security Trends Global Impact Analysis (CSTGIA) 2026 series, we explore why the future belongs to organizations that don't simply anticipate disruption, but continuously adapt before disruption overtakes them.

This session introduces the concept of the Adaptive Cyber Enterprise, where cybersecurity becomes an enterprise-wide capability built on continuous learning, workforce evolution, AI-enabled collaboration, knowledge management, and adaptive leadership.

In this episode, you'll learn:
✅ Why adaptation has become the new competitive advantage
✅ The difference between Strategic Cyber Foresight and Adaptive Cyber Enterprises
✅ Five leadership moves that strengthen long-term cyber resilience
✅ How AI, knowledge management, and workforce capability create sustainable advantage
✅ Why continuous learning is becoming strategic infrastructure
✅ Practical questions every executive should ask to assess organizational readiness

Whether you're a CEO, CIO, CISO, CTO, Chief Risk Officer, Board Member, Program Executive, Government Leader, Cybersecurity Professional, or Digital Transformation Executive, this discussion provides practical insights into preparing your organization for an increasingly AI-enabled and rapidly changing future.

Key Topics

• Artificial Intelligence

• Cybersecurity Leadership
• Workforce Transformation

name: Bat Walk at the Susquehannock Wildlife Conservation Center
description:
Join the Susquehannock Wildlife Society for an evening of bats! 

We’ll start with a short screening of Beneficial Bats by Marty Stouffer, then head outside for a guided walk around the Conservation Center grounds to listen for, detect, and identify bats. Along the way, we'll collect citizen science data on the bats we detect and talk about our local bat species, their conservation status, and how you can support them!

The walk is led by Sadie Rozics, a Wildlife Conservation Technician with the Susquehannock Wildlife Society through the Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps. Sadie has studied bats in Owings Mills and will guide the group using an ultrasonic bat detector, which picks up bat echolocation calls that people can't normally hear and plays them back as sound. We'll stop at several points along the route to listen, take turns at the detector, and record what we find.

Regular attendance at these classes can assist kids with the development of important life skills such as increased empathy, respect for others, self control and concentration.

name: Carole Boston Weatherford: "Fourteen Ways of Looking at Jellyfish"
description:
A graceful bundle of nerves three times as ancient as the dinosaurs, the jellyfish is no fish but a spineless invertebrate without brain, heart, blood, or bones. Inside glass tanks in crowded aquariums, jellies hold visitors rapt with their slow-motion water ballet. Most of the world’s nearly four thousand species emit an otherworldly light, glowing red, yellow, violet, or blue in the underwater dark. Fifty species boast deadly venom, including pink meanies with boa-like tentacles, box jellies with two-dozen eyes apiece, and deadliest of all, cubozoans the size of human thumbnails. Coretta Scott King Award–winning author Carole Boston Weatherford brings poetry and playfulness to natural science as she shares her fascination with a singular creature. Fourteen wildly divergent poems—by turns dramatic and serene—pulse with life. From spreads of shimmering bioluminescence to graphic panels, stylish artwork blends poetry with science and fact with folklore and myth to form the ideal introduction to the “immortal” and mysterious jellyfish.

 

About the Author:

Carole Boston Weatherford is a New York Times bestselling author of 60-plus books including the Caldecott Honor book Unspeakable: The Tulsa Race Massacre, for which she was also awarded the Coretta Scott King Author Award and a Sibert Honor; the Newbery Honor winner Box; and the Caldecott Honor winners Freedom in Congo Square, Fannie Lou Hamer, and Moses. She won a Coretta Scott King Author Honor for Becoming Billie Holiday. Weatherford teaches composition and children's literature at Fayetteville State University in North Carolina. Visit cbweatherford.com.

name: From Cost Barriers to Circular Assets: Policy & Operational Models for EV Battery Recycling
description: As electric vehicles and stationary energy storage units become more common, managing end-of-life batteries presents direct operational and financial challenges. In many regions, salvage yards and local dismantlers face high processing and transport fees for large format batteries, leaving them hesitant to accept battery systems or entire vehicles without clear cost-effective management pathways. Join industry speakers for a practical discussion on how state policy, processing innovations, and industry advocacy are coming together to address these cost barriers and keep valuable critical minerals in circulation. This session will explore Colorado’s landmark legislation that brought automakers, recyclers, and auto dismantlers into a balanced framework, Cirba Solutions' operational approaches to EV battery processing economics and scale, and the Recycled Materials Association’s (ReMA) work to promote safe EV and lithium-ion battery recycling through advocacy, safety training, and public education.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: The Life of Frankenstein
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“The Life of Frankenstein,”** on the birth, evolution and impact of a tale of man-made monstrosity, with Bernard Welt, an emeritus professor of arts and humanities at George Washington University who frequently lectures on Frankenstein in literature, cinema, and culture.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-life-of-frankenstein](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-life-of-frankenstein) .]

Guillermo del Toro’s lush and lovingly produced film adaptation of Mary Shelley’s 1818 novel *Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus* is just the latest of many iterations of the story to capture the public’s imagination. People have watched Victor Frankenstein give life to his monster in numerous films, on television, and on stage, and even perform “Putting on the Ritz” with him thanks to the comic genius of Mel Brooks.

Mary Shelley did not just tell a tale. She spawned the modern genre of speculative fiction and gave rise to a myth that would crop up in debates over nature versus nurture and other matters. Even today it stokes anxieties over the potential impacts of robotics, artificial intelligence, and genetic engineering, by evoking the image of a monster turning on its progenitor.

Come gain a new appreciation of Mary Shelley’s creation with the help of Dr. Bernard Welt, who has studied the relationship between nightmares and the horror genre and is the author of *Mythomania: Fantasies, Fables, and Sheer Lies in Contemporary American Popular Art.*

Dr. Welt will start by telling a literary origin story almost as famous as Frankenstein itself, of how an 18-year-old Shelley started writing Frankenstein in 1816 while staying in a villa on Lake Geneva with two of her era’s leading poets, Lord Byron and Percy Bysshe Shelley, her lover. Housebound by foul weather, the three read Gothic tales of ghosts and monsters and challenged each other to produce something even more terrifying. Mary dreamed up a story of a man who defied death by creating a living being out of scraps of deceased men harvested from graveyards and anatomy labs.

The resulting novel, *Frankenstein*, published anonymously in 1818, would by that century’s end become a touchstone in philosophical discourse on the nature of humanity and in political discussions of imperialism and populism. By the 21st century, Mary Shelley (as she became) had earned a more significant place in the literary canon than Byron and her husband Shelley.

We will examine how this grisly tale became a landmark of modern thought and look at the part played by numerous film adaptations from the first years of cinema to the present day. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID. Bar doors open at 5 pm. The talk starts at 6:30.)

Image: From a Theodor von Holst engraving in an 1831 edition of Frankenstein published by Colburn and Bentley of London.

name: Riley Black: "Tyrant Lizard Queen"
description:
From the author of the beloved The Last Days of the Dinosaurs, an imaginative celebration of T. rex from hatching to adulthood

 

Tyrannosaurus rex is a prehistoric celebrity. Exceeding 40 feet in length and weighing over 9 tons, the largest individuals of this dinosaurian species were intimidating predators capable of crushing bone and consuming more than a hundred pounds of flesh in a bite. But the last of the tyrant dinosaurs had a life beyond ripping and tearing. More than 66 million years ago, T. rex courted each other, nested, watched over their offspring, slept, drank, and explored ancient floodplains inhabited by a fantastic cast of impressive dinosaurs like the huge long-neck Alamosaurus and burly, three-horned Torosaurus. For the first time, the life story of this impressive, sensitive predator is told as if you were there to watch it unfold.

 

In her latest prehistoric nature walk, bestselling and award-winning author Riley Black follows the life of plucky T. rex Snaggletooth from the time she hatches through her tumultuous adulthood. The prehistoric forest Snag emerges into is full of danger, and yet, as Riley weaves the latest fossil discoveries into the story, the carnivorous dinosaur survives to play, court, fight, sleep, nest, and more as she grows up in Cretaceous North America. She tussles with rival tyrannosaurs, hunts for delectable prey, and finds soft moments of connection in the forest. Even the most die-hard dinosaur fan will come away with a new perspective and appreciation for the Tyrant Lizard Queen.

 

Riley Black will be joined in conversation by WYPR's Senior News Analyst Tom Hall. 

 

About the Author: 

RILEY BLACK (she/they) has been heralded as “one of our premier gifted young science writers” and is the bestselling, award-winning author of several books, including When the Earth Was Green and The Last Days of the Dinosaurs. A science correspondent for Smithsonian and regular contributor to publications like National Geographic and Slate, Riley is a widely-recognized expert on paleontology. She won the 2024 Friend of Darwin Award from the National Center for Science Education.

 

About the Moderator: 

Tom Hall is WYPR's Senior News Analyst. He was the host of Midday, the award-winning, highly rated news and public policy program on WYPR Radio that featured interviews with elected officials, community leaders, as well as thought provoking authors, artists, researchers, journalists and scholars from around the world.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: The Haunted House
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“The Haunted House,”** on scary dwellings and their grip on us, with Brittany Warman, former instructor at Ohio State University and co-founder of The Carterhaugh School of Folklore and the Fantastic.

[Doors open at 5. The talk starts at 6:30. The room is open seating. Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-the-haunted-house ](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-the-haunted-house )]

The haunted house has long held a place in the imaginations of those who enjoy a bit of uncanny terror, posing the ultimate threat to security and normalcy. It’s where something familiar becomes strange and unsettling, even threatening. You initially might have thought you're safe—after all, you should be safe indoors—but you're not. Sanctuary and shelter have turned against you. The very walls trouble your dreams.

Come tour some of the most terrifying real estate ever imagined with Brittany Warman, who has earned herself a large and devoted following among Profs and Pints audiences with excellent past talks on folklore, fairy tales, and horror.

She’ll show you the fascinating folkloric, literary, and real-world history of the haunted house. She’ll leave you wondering about the creepy old places in your town with doors that you’re afraid to approach on Halloween, and she might even leave you eager to turn your own home into such an eerie dwelling.

She’ll begin by discussing the scary structures of fairy tales, such as gingerbread houses and Bluebeard's castle, exploring how the early stories told about them influenced the terrifying tales of Henry James' Bly Manor and Edgar Allen Poe's House of Usher. She’ll consider the impact of haunted spaces on the Gothic and horror genres and explain why haunted houses are often so opulent and so decadent in their decay.

Among the questions Dr. Warman will tackle: What might the haunted house have to say about history, culture, and society? What draws us, again and again, to haunted houses, making us want to visit them, find their ghosts, and uncover their stories?

She'll conclude by examining how these tales still resonate today, in haunted houses both purportedly real and those decidedly fake, meant for shocks and thrills. Even Disney's Haunted Mansion ride will make an appearance. It’s a scary world after all. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID.)

Image: An abandoned house near Pocomoke City, Md., in 2008. (Photo by Matt Trostle / Creative Commons.)

description:
About the Event

Living with chronic illness can be isolating — especially when it feels like no one truly understands what you’re going through. That’s why we created Chronically ChILL, a social group for chronically ill people who just want to connect, talk, and be themselves.

Our socials are a relaxed, judgment-free space to simply be human and enjoy the company of others who get it. There’s no agenda, no pressure, and no need to talk about symptoms unless you want to. It’s just about making friends, laughing a little, and finding community.

Come as you are — camera optional, pajama friendly, cozy vibes welcome.

⸻

What to Expect
• Easygoing conversation and good company
• A warm, understanding community
• Zero pressure to perform or overshare
• The chance to actually socialize and make new friends who understand the ups and downs of chronic illness

Whether you join for ten minutes or the full hour, you’re part of the ChILL community.

***In order to join the Zoom call, your zoom username MUST match your Meetup name.***

⸻
☕ What to Bring
• Yourself, exactly as you are
• Snacks or drinks if you'd like
⸻

Who It’s For

Chronically ill, disabled, and neurodivergent individuals looking for friendship, laughter, and connection in a relaxed online environment.

You don’t have to be “doing well” to show up — you just have to show up.

name: NEC Drop-in: BOOtiful Bats
description:
October’s theme, Nocturnal Animals of Cylburn, focuses on animals that become active as the sun goes down. Each Saturday will highlight a different nocturnal animal that calls Cylburn Arboretum home and explore the adaptations that help them thrive at night. While some creatures of the night sometimes get a spooky reputation, we’ll shed some light on these often misunderstood animals and discover there’s much more to admire than fear!

Please note: NO live animals will be present during these programs.

All ages are welcome. No fee or registration required (supplies limited). Drop-in anytime between 11am to 12pm.

October 3: Observant Owls

Whooo’s awake when the sun goes down? Drop by the Nature Education Center to discover the owls that call Cylburn home and uncover the adaptations that make these nighttime hunters so well suited for life after dark. 

October 10: Remarkable Raccoons

There’s a ‘masked’ visitor roaming Cylburn after dark! A raccoon’s distinctive black mask provides camouflage and helps reduce glare. Drop by the Nature Education Center to find out more about the adaptations that help them thrive at night.

October 17: Fantastic Flying squirrels

Something is soaring through the trees but it isn’t a bird or a bat! Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about how these small nocturnal mammals glide through the forest after dark. 

October 24: Outstanding Opossums

What’s lurking around Cylburn after dark? It might be an opossum!  Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about the only marsupials in North America and how they help the environment.

October 31: BOOtiful Bats

This Halloween, discover the bats that fly over Cylburn after sunset. Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn how these nocturnal mammals navigate the darkness and play an important role in our ecosystem.

name: W29 CSTGIA 2026: From Strategic Cyber Foresight to Adaptive Cyber Enterprises
description:
### From Adaptive Cyber Enterprises to Anticipatory Cyber Leadership: Shaping the Future Before Others Recognize It

What separates organizations that merely adapt from those that shape the future?

In this episode of Creating Something That Gives It All Away (CSTGIA), we explore the next evolution of executive leadership: Anticipatory Cyber Leadership. As artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, cybersecurity threats, and digital transformation accelerate, organizations can no longer afford to simply react to disruption, they must learn to anticipate emerging trends, engineer opportunity, and prepare for futures that have not yet arrived.

Together, we'll examine the five leadership shifts that distinguish tomorrow's leaders from today's managers, including moving from adaptation to anticipation, risk management to opportunity engineering, AI assistance to executive decision intelligence, strategic planning to continuous future design, and organizational learning to ecosystem leadership. Discover how leaders can strengthen strategic curiosity, systems thinking, decision intelligence, human-AI collaboration, and learning velocity to build organizations that don't just survive change, they create it.

In this episode you'll learn:
(1) Why leadership, not technology, is becoming the greatest competitive advantage
(2) The five leadership shifts driving anticipatory organizations
(3) How AI can strengthen executive decision-making without replacing human judgment
(4) Practical strategies for preparing your organization before disruption occurs
(5) How to develop the mindset and capabilities needed to shape the future instead of reacting to it

🎥 **Watch on YouTube:** https://youtu.be/tUazH_33CGs

If you enjoy this content, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to help others prepare for the future of cybersecurity, leadership, and digital transformation.

🔔 New episodes of CSTGIA 2026 are released weekly, exploring the emerging trends, technologies, leadership strategies, and enterprise capabilities shaping the future of cybersecurity and organizational excellence.

name: Christopher Freeburg: "Soul"
description:
How did enslaved Africans turn America’s infamous failure into the greatest moral occasion of modern Western life? In this book, Christopher Freeburg answers that question with one word: soul. It was soul, Freeburg believes, which drove Black individuals and communities, grappling with horrific strife, to reimagine American life and equality in earnest.

 

Black cultural life contains a central and significant theme—a soul, or form of life—expressed in a variety of musical, religious, and political forms. Through the work and words of figures ranging from the poet Phillis Wheatley to President Barack Obama and musician Nina Simone to disco owner Jewel Thais-Williams, Freeburg shows how Black communities leaned time and again on soul and its four pillars: resonance, revelation, resilience, and transcendence. It is soul, what Freeburg calls a beautiful transaction between individual and community across time and place, that has allowed Black people over generations to transform feelings of defeat and alienation into moral courage and shared belonging.

 

Christopher Freeburg will be joined in conversation by The Atlantic's senior editor Vann Newkirk. 

 

About the Author: 

Christopher Freeburg is the Presidential Humanities and Social Sciences Chair in English at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign. His most recent book was Counterlife: Slavery after Resistance and Social Death.

 

About the Moderator: 

Vann Newkirk is a senior editor at The Atlantic and the host of the podcasts Floodlines and Holy Week.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 6 pm. A local bookseller will be on-site and have books available for purchase.Free parking vouchers are available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) after 4pm.  Ask Pratt event staff for your parking voucher prior to or after the program. This free event will be presented in-person and virtually.   This is a seated event with spaces reserved for individuals with accessibility needs. ASL interpretation will also be available for attendees throughout the event. If you need additional accommodations to successfully participate, please let us know at events@prattlibrary.org or 443-768-0762.

name: WP Site Management Tools
description:
A common question that comes up repeatedly is "what is the best tool to manage websites for ME". Cause different people have different needs.

We've invited the 3 main players in the "done for you" WP management and we'll interview them about their features so that you can compare them in a more "apples to apples" way and make your own decision about what's best for you.

The tools:
\- ManageWP\, WP Remote\, and WP Umbrella are confirmed\.

The topics:

\- Backups & restoration
\- Manual & automated updates
\- Plugin/theme management across sites
\- User management \(both on the tool & on WP sites\)
\- Security/vulnerability
\- Reports
\- Broken links/Performance/Uptime/Site health monitoring
\- AI
\- GDPR & privacy compliance
\- Any other special features

The format:

10 topics, each tool gets 2 min to talk about what they do for the topic. So people can listen to topics that matter most to them and get the three tools one after the other.

I'll introduce the topic, ie: Backups & restoration with a 15-30 second intro then each product owner gets 2 minutes to talk about their product and their product ONLY.

You'll be muted on entry, we'll be using the chat to queue people up/ask follow-on questions.

The meetup is scheduled for 11am ET until 12:30pm ET.

Meetup is scheduled to be recorded. Recordings are posted about 2 weeks after the meetup and are provided courtesy of our sponsor, [Obee Digital Consulting](https://obeedigitalconsulting.com/).

How to get notified about the recording: either subscribe to the [youtube channel](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoT0wv53Bj-BGfD8fPhMRC3qTtPMZHioI), RSVP "yes" to the meetup, or [join the mailing list](https://share.mailercloud.com/form?id=a0NzdUAxMTI1OUAwMDAwMA==).

threadHOURS

Ask what they’re excited about, what feels challenging, and what would help them start the year strong. Come to threadHOURS together to make a plan, tackle a next step, or connect with someone who can help.

name: Timothy Tyson and Mary Williams: "Mahalia Jackson, Moving on Up a Little Higher"
description:
If Americans today still recognize the name Mahalia Jackson, they might recall that she was perhaps the greatest gospel singer who ever lived. But for many people, there is no awareness at all, not even for an entertainer whose “Move On Up a Little Higher” sold eight million copies, who headlined two Newport Jazz Festivals and performed before four United States presidents.

 

While this rich musical legacy is admired by those in the know, virtually no one recognizes Jackson’s astonishing role in American civil rights history. In this startling new depiction of the renowned gospel singer, New York Times best-selling author Timothy B. Tyson and Mary D. Williams, an acclaimed gospel singer herself, bring Jackson back to soaring life by positioning her as the major civil rights figure she, in fact, was.

 

Mahlia Jackson, Moving On Up a Little Higher then traces Jackson’s career from abject poverty in New Orleans to global superstardom, revealing how even after meteoric success, Jackson maintained an unwavering devotion to Black freedom. In the 1930s in Chicago, even before the Civil Rights Movement took its modern shape, she used her rapturous voice to support independent Black political power. Her work only intensified in the 1940s and beyond when she campaigned first for Franklin D. Roosevelt, and later for Harry Truman, John F. Kennedy, and Lyndon B. Johnson; headlined in Montgomery for the 1955–56 bus boycott; sang for the Birmingham campaign and on the Selma March; and performed at the iconic 1963 March on Washington, where she urged Martin Luther King Jr. to “Tell ’em about the dream.” In retrospect what becomes historically significant is that Mahalia Jackson was present at so many civil rights events, even singing a divine rendition of “Precious Lord, Take My Hand,” at Dr. King’s funeral in 1968. Weakened and worn, she succumbed to heart failure four years later at the age of sixty.

 

Weaving together Mahalia Jackson’s inspiring life journey with her soulful music into a transcendent text, this biography ultimately casts Mahalia Jackson as we’ve never seen her before, as a guiding light for the Civil Rights Movement, whose message still speaks to our struggles today.

 

Timothy B. Tyson and Mary D. Williams will be joined in conversation by The Atlantic's senior editor Vann Newkirk. 

 

About the Authors: 

Timothy B. Tyson is senior research scholar at the Center for Documentary Studies at Duke University and the author of five books, including New York Times bestseller The Blood of Emmett Till.

 

Mary D. Williams is a gospel singer, civil rights historian, and former adjunct professor at Duke University. She has performed at the Kennedy Center and the Metropolitan Museum of Art and lives in Garner, North Carolina.

 

About the Moderator: 

Vann Newkirk is a senior editor at The Atlantic and the host of the podcasts Floodlines and Holy Week.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 6 pm. A local bookseller will be on-site and have books available for purchase.Free parking vouchers are available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) after 4pm.  Ask Pratt event staff for your parking voucher prior to or after the program. This free event will be presented in-person and virtually.   This is a seated event with spaces reserved for individuals with accessibility needs. ASL interpretation will also be available for attendees throughout the event. If you need additional accommodations to successfully participate, please let us know at events@prattlibrary.org or 443-768-0762.

Artificial intelligence is becoming ubiquitous. Autonomous systems are proliferating. Data is abundant. Yet many organizations still struggle with fragmented decisions, disconnected knowledge, and organizational silos.

In this week's Cyber & STEAM Global Innovation Alliance (CSTGIA) Spotlight on What's Next 2026 – Week 30, Dr. Rhonda Farrell explores the next evolution of cybersecurity leadership: the transition from Anticipatory Cyber Leadership to Cognitive Cyber Enterprises.

In this session you'll learn:
• Why enterprise intelligence is becoming the next competitive advantage
• The five strategic moves toward Cognitive Cyber Enterprises
• How connected decisions outperform connected databases
• Why AI must orchestrate knowledge—not simply automate tasks

The organizations that lead tomorrow won't simply deploy smarter technology, they'll build enterprises that become smarter every single day.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: How Ancient Athens Restored Democracy
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“How Ancient Athens Restored Democracy,”** on lessons to be learned from an overthrow of tyrants in 403 B.C., with Nicholas D. Cross, assistant professor of history at the United States Naval Academy and author of *The Roots of Cooperation: Constructing Interstate Alliances in Ancient Greece.*

[Doors open at 3. The talk starts at 4:30. The room is open seating. Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-athens-democracy](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-athens-democracy) ]

The defeat of Athens in the Peloponnesian War led to its democracy being replaced by the Thirty Tyrants, an oligarchic regime that consolidated power through executions and political repression. Democratic exiles managed to organize resistance, defeat the oligarchic forces, and return to Athens to restore democratic government, but then faced the far more challenging task of reconciling a community torn apart by political divisions.

The restorers of Athenian democracy grappled with a question that often arises in periods of political upheaval: Can a deeply divided community ever overcome its past and build a shared future? Learn how they managed to bring about such an outcome in a talk that holds hopeful lessons for our own time.

The speaker, Dr. Nicholas Cross, teaches the history of ancient Greece and Rome and is the author of a forthcoming biography of the leader of democratic resistance to the *Thirty Tyrants, Thrasybulus of Steiria: An Athenian Hero?*

He’ll describe how the settlement that followed the civil war included an amnesty designed to prevent cycles of retaliation, but Athens nonetheless remained deeply divided. Among those who had to find a way to live together once more were former democrats, supporters of oligarchy, and citizens such as Socrates whose conduct during the regime was open to question.

Democracy’s return was not a straightforward triumph. It instead involved dealing with tensions and making political decisions intended to enable peaceful coexistence possible. The Athenians had to balance both accountability with reconciliation and the desire for revenge with the need for lasting political stability.

The events of 403 BC remind us that rebuilding a divided society requires not only restoring political institutions but also reviving trust and learning to coexist with former adversaries. The lessons they learned in the process remain relevant nearly 2500 years later. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID.)

Image: The Acropolis at Athens as painted by Leo von Klenze in 1846 (Neue Pinakothek museum / Wikimedia Commons).

name: Paula Chase: "Off Balance"
description:
Gossip is juicier, secrets are bigger, and tensions are higher than ever in this riveting sequel to Balancing Act.

 

Hot Lipz, everyone’s favorite–or least favorite–Chatter account is back at it, stirring up gossip among the rival schools in Da Icy City. Selena knows that it’s only a matter of time before she finds herself on the other end of the rumors—and she has a secret.

 

While Selena sets out to uncover Hot Lipz’s true identity, Leesh is still reeling from the account’s last big reveal: she has a sister, and it’s none other than her biggest gymnastics rival, Chyna. Now somebody from Leesh’s past is calling in a favor, and if anyone finds out, it could ruin everything she’s worked for.

 

The pressure is on as the Power Panthers Gymnastics team prepares to compete in the Diamond Cup, and with a new student arriving at the Heights, loyalties will be tested like never before.

Paula Chase is the co-founder of the award-winning blog, The Brown Bookshelf. She is a longtime advocate for diversifying the type of fiction featuring Black characters. Chase is the author of nine critically acclaimed upper middle grade and YA novels and a winner of NCTE’s Assembly on Literature for Adolescents (ALAN) Konigsberg Award.

About:

Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
Fall Focus: Starting Strong — School, Service Year & What Comes Next!
Fall is a season of new beginnings! As young people head back to
school, college, training programs, and work — and our newest Maryland Corps / Service Year members begin their year of service —
TouchPoint
threadHOURS
is here to help everyone start strong and stay on track.
Each Wednesday at threadHOURS, young people can get hands-on support navigating the opportunities and challenges that come with a new school or program year. Whether they need help adjusting to a new schedule, staying on top of school or Service Year expectations, connecting to resources, solving a problem before it becomes a barrier, or thinking ahead to their next academic or professional step, threadHOURS is a place to check in, get connected, and keep moving forward.
For our
Maryland Corps / Service Year members
, threadHOURS is also a place to stay connected throughout the year — celebrating wins, troubleshooting challenges at their host sites, accessing additional resources and opportunities, and making sure their year of service is building toward what comes next.
How you can roll as a volunteer:

name: W31 CSTGIA 2026: Cognitive Cyber Enterprises
description:
### When AI Can Act Independently\, Trust Must Become an Enterprise System \| CSTGIA Week 31

What happens when AI stops simply recommending what humans should do—and begins acting on our behalf?

Welcome to CSTGIA 2026 Week 31: From Cognitive Cyber Enterprises to Autonomous Trust Ecosystems.

Agentic AI is rapidly changing the cybersecurity and governance equation. Intelligent agents can execute multi-step workflows, interact with other systems, access organizational information, make decisions, and take actions with increasing autonomy.
That means we are moving from protecting systems people operate toward assuring systems that increasingly operate themselves.

And that requires something bigger than cybersecurity alone.
It requires trust architecture.

In this episode, Dr. Rhonda Farrell explores five critical shifts leaders should be preparing for: moving from identity management to agent identity, periodic compliance to continuous assurance, human approval to intelligent guardrails, organizational security to ecosystem trust, and incident response to trust recovery.

The defining leadership question is no longer simply:
“Do we trust our AI?” It is: “Can our ecosystem continuously prove why trust is warranted?”

⚙️ This Week’s Challenge
Choose one AI-enabled workflow and map its trust chain: Human → Data → AI → Decision → Action → System → Outcome → Accountability

Then ask: Where does that chain become invisible?
That invisible point may be tomorrow’s risk.

Cybersecurity protects systems. Governance establishes boundaries. Assurance validates performance. But autonomous trust ecosystems make something even more important possible: responsible autonomy at scale.

The organizations that lead the intelligent era won’t necessarily have the most autonomous technology. They will build ecosystems in which technology, people, partners, governance, and communities can trust one another at scale.

🎥 **Watch on YouTube:** https://youtu.be/cjP0btuUWUo

If you enjoy this content, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to help others prepare for the future of cybersecurity, leadership, and digital transformation.

🔔 New episodes of CSTGIA 2026 are released weekly, exploring the emerging trends, technologies, leadership strategies, and enterprise capabilities shaping the future of cybersecurity and organizational excellence.

#CSTGIA #Cybersecurity #AgenticAI #ResponsibleAI #DigitalTrust #AIGovernance #CyberResilience #AutonomousSystems #ArtificialIntelligence #FutureOfCybersecurity

name: Tame PyTorch Recompiles & Unlock Jev GPU Throughput with Zymtrace
description:
**Monday, November 16, 2026 · 9:00–10:00 AM PST · Online**
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
Join us for two deep dives into hidden AI performance costs: surprise PyTorch recompilations during inference and compute, memory, and communication bottlenecks in Jev training.
**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads**
by Chaim Rand
`torch.compile` can accelerate steady-state inference, yet a guard failure on a new input shape or layout can trigger an expensive recompilation in the request path. Drawing on his latest post, Chaim will compare six approaches using a dynamic graph-neural-network example: cache preloading, bounded recompilation with eager fallback, Dynamo and input-layout tuning, warmup seeding, background compilation, and ahead-of-time compilation with `torch.export` and AOTInductor. He’ll explain their tradeoffs and how the right choice depends on the model, input distribution, runtime environment, and latency requirements.
**Bio:** Chaim Rand is a machine-learning algorithm developer who writes about PyTorch and practical AI/ML performance optimization.
**Based on:** [Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads](https://chaimrand.medium.com/overcoming-the-pytorch-recompilation-dilemma-in-real-time-inference-workloads-069fac5485cd)
**Talk #2: From Profiles to Throughput: How TypeSafe Optimized Jev with Zymtrace**
by Israel Ogbole, Co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace
Israel will explore the latest Zymtrace/TypeSafe case study on training and serving Jev. He’ll discuss how continuous CPU/GPU profiling and MCP-accessible profile data supported an iterative optimization loop across compute, memory, communication, and inference synchronization. The published case study reports approximately 46% higher training throughput on the same hardware after three successive changes, plus approximately 10% better inference performance after removing a hidden device-to-host synchronization. The talk will focus on how the team found each bottleneck, measured each change, and identified the next constraint.
**Bio:** Israel Ogbole is co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace, which develops continuous CPU/GPU profiling tools for performance optimization.
**Based on:** [How TypeSafe achieved 46% higher GPU throughput training Jev — with the help of Zymtrace](https://zymtrace.com/article/typesafe-zymtrace/)
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
**Related Links**
Github Repo: [http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/](http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/)

name: Rachel Beanland: "The Half Life"
description:
When twenty-three-year-old Eileen O’Malley meets charismatic naval officer Paul Archer in a Charleston department store, she doesn’t expect to fall so hard, so fast. But Paul is funny and ambitious, and soon, Eileen’s got a ring on her finger and is following him to the tiny, sun-drenched Mediterranean island of La Maddalena, where Paul will be heading up Radiological Controls aboard a submarine tender.

 

In La Maddalena, Eileen joins a makeshift community of navy wives who are hell-bent on making the island feel a little more like home. But for Eileen, whose brother died in Vietnam, home is a loaded word, and as she settles into life on the island—taking Italian lessons and learning to make culurgiones—she begins to love the place for all the ways it is not like where she comes from.

 

Still, it doesn’t take long for Eileen to be confronted with the complexities of being an American abroad. The decision to send nuclear-powered subs into the La Maddalena Archipelago was a contentious one, and the U.S. government is doing whatever it can to ensure that the island—not to mention all of Italy—doesn’t go communist in the next election.

 

When Italian activists and scientists begin to sound the alarm about possible nuclear contamination in the water, the island erupts in a series of protests, made worse by the ongoing mishaps of the U.S. Navy. Soon, Eileen’s marriage falters and her loyalties begin to shift as she is drawn into a web of secrets—and to a local journalist who forces her to imagine a life beyond the one she’s been handed.

 

Atmospheric, sexy, and quietly defiant, The Half Life is a story of love, complicity, and awakening—of one woman forced to choose between loyalty to her husband and country and to the Italian locals who show her the high cost of American exceptionalism.

 

About the Author: 

Rachel Beanland is the author of The House Is on Fire and Florence Adler Swims Forever, which won the National Jewish Book Award for Debut Fiction. She is a graduate of the University of South Carolina and earned her MFA in creative writing from Virginia Commonwealth University. She lives with her family in Richmond, Virginia.

description:

Location:

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
Fall Focus: Starting Strong — School, Service Year & What Comes Next!
Fall is a season of new beginnings! As young people head back to
school, college, training programs, and work — and our newest Maryland Corps / Service Year members begin their year of service —
TouchPoint
threadHOURS
is here to help everyone start strong and stay on track.
Each Wednesday at threadHOURS, young people can get hands-on support navigating the opportunities and challenges that come with a new school or program year. Whether they need help adjusting to a new schedule, staying on top of school or Service Year expectations, connecting to resources, solving a problem before it becomes a barrier, or thinking ahead to their next academic or professional step, threadHOURS is a place to check in, get connected, and keep moving forward.
For our
Maryland Corps / Service Year members
, threadHOURS is also a place to stay connected throughout the year — celebrating wins, troubleshooting challenges at their host sites, accessing additional resources and opportunities, and making sure their year of service is building toward what comes next.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
The beginning of a new school, work, or service year is a great time to reconnect with your young person. Ask what they’re excited about, what feels challenging, and what would help them start the year strong. Come to threadHOURS together to make a plan, tackle a next step, or connect with someone who can help.
You don’t need to have all the answers — showing up, asking questions, and helping your young person navigate the transition is exactly the relational scaffolding they need.
